forward_citation_audit:
## Outcome

**No explicit resolution of the exact higher-dimensional, all-Jordan-set density question was found in this bounded audit. This does not establish priority or certify that the question remains open.** I independently inspected the three OpenAlex-indexed citing works and identified one important later, second-hop result.

### Original paper and journal-version status

**Faustin Adiceam and Ioannis Tsokanos, “Higher dimensional spiral Delone sets.”**

- Latest arXiv version: **[2010.06428v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.06428), 30 March 2021**. Read introduction, definitions, and §6, pp.22–23; the explicit density question is present.
- Refereed version: **Functiones et Approximatio Commentarii Mathematici 67(1), 21–46 (2022)**, **[DOI 10.7169/facm/1958](https://doi.org/10.7169/facm/1958)**. [Crossref](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.7169/facm/1958) records publication on **14 September 2022**; OpenAlex’s April date corresponds to earlier metadata/advance-publication timing.
- **Journal retention or alteration of §6 is unverified.** Project Euclid’s PDF, full-text and short-record endpoints all returned bot-block pages. The [HAL journal record](https://hal.science/hal-04263148) links only to the arXiv manuscript, not a separate accepted/published PDF. Publisher contents confirm the article’s placement but do not expose its concluding section. I therefore cannot transfer the arXiv question’s wording to the journal version.

### Additional later result missed by stopping at those three

**Yohay Ailon Tevet, “Chabauty Limits of Fermat Spirals.”** [arXiv:2506.22863v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.22863), **16 September 2025**; *Combinatorics and Number Theory* **14(3–4),239–249 (2025)**, [DOI 10.2140/cnt.2025.14.239](https://msp.org/cnt/2025/14-3/p02.xhtml).

This is a **second-hop citation through the visibility paper**, not a direct citation of the target. Read §§1–2, Proposition 12’s density discussion, “Further Questions,” and bibliography.

- **Corollary 7, p.4:** “No Fermat spiral is a dense forest.”
- This explicitly answers the **planar sunflower visibility question**.
- It **does not** settle higher-dimensional angular uniform distribution. Its density discussion concerns origin-ball counts and planar lattice covolumes, not the target’s every-Jordan-set criterion.

## Additional coverage and limitations

- Read current publication lists of **[Adiceam](https://sites.google.com/site/fadiceammaths/research)**, **[Tsokanos](https://sites.google.com/view/ioannis-tsokanos)** and **[Akiyama](http://math.tsukuba.ac.jp/~akiyama/Research2reverse.html)**. None listed a further explicitly identified resolution. These lists are discovery evidence, not completeness certificates.
- **Tsokanos’s [2022 Manchester thesis](https://pure.manchester.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/224503987/FULL_TEXT.PDF):** read contents, publications statement and selected Chapter 4 passages; searched its extracted text. It incorporates referee revisions but is **not evidence that the journal retained §6**.
- Searched exact title/identifier, density/equidistribution terminology, and norm-ordering/radial-rescaling/rank-adjustment terminology. **No matching construction was located**; negative searches do not establish novelty.
- Google Scholar lookup and title search both returned **403**. Adiceam’s 2023 HDR metadata was accessible, but its PDF retrieval failed; no substantive status claim rests on it. No paywall bypass, external writes, code or tests were used.
classical_bound_and_prior_construction_a:
## Finding

**The required discrepancy estimate is classical and directly supported for every fixed \(n\ge2\).** For balls, its history predates Hlawka. I found **no verified prior construction that sorts all nonzero lattice vectors by Euclidean norm and moves the \(k\)-th vector to radius \(k^{1/n}\)**. This bounded search does **not** establish priority.

## Load-bearing sources

1. **Jingwei Guo, “Lattice points in rotated convex domains,” published version, 2015**, *Revista Matemática Iberoamericana* **31**(2), 411–438. DOI: **[10.4171/rmi/839](https://doi.org/10.4171/rmi/839)**; [publisher PDF](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/38537).  
   **Read depth:** introduction, relevant smoothing passages, bibliography—not the complete proof.  
   **Exact locator:** §1, p.411. For a compact convex domain \(B\subset\mathbb R^d\), \(d\ge2\), containing the origin in its interior, with smooth boundary and everywhere positive Gaussian curvature, it states
   \[
   P_B(t)=\#(tB\cap\mathbb Z^d)-|B|t^d
          =O\!\left(t^{d-2+2/(d+1)}\right),\qquad t\ge1.
   \]
   It attributes this standard estimate to Hlawka [6]. Euclidean closed unit balls meet every hypothesis. This is the cleanest single citation covering **all requested dimensions**, without averaging, exceptional radii, rotations, or an added \(\varepsilon\).

2. **Edmund Hlawka, “Über Integrale auf konvexen Körpern I,” 1950**, *Monatshefte für Mathematik* **54**, 1–36. DOI: **[10.1007/BF01304101](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01304101)**.  
   **Read depth:** publisher bibliographic record only; full text was subscription content and was not accessed. Guo’s reference [6] independently identifies this paper. **Do not claim a directly inspected theorem number from Hlawka.**

3. **A. Ivić, E. Krätzel, M. Kühleitner, W. G. Nowak, “Lattice points in large regions and related arithmetic functions: Recent developments in a very classic topic,” arXiv:math/0410522v1, 25 October 2004** ([PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0410522)).  
   **Read depth:** §§1–2, targeted §3.2 passages and relevant bibliography.  
   **Exact locators:** §3.2, pp.16–17, “Ellipsoids”; references [104], [107]. For an arbitrary positive-definite real quadratic form \(F^2\) in \(p\ge3\) variables, it gives
   \[
   \#\{m:F(m)\le x\}
   =\frac{\pi^{p/2}}{\Gamma(p/2+1)\sqrt{\det A}}x^p
     +O(x^{p-2+2/(p+1)}).
   \]
   Verbatim: **“hold for arbitrary ellipsoids.”** It attributes this to **Landau, 1915 and 1924**. Reference [104] is *Zur analytischen Zahlentheorie der definiten quadratischen Formen (Ueber die Gitterpunkte in einem mehrdimensionalen Ellipsoid)*, *Sitzber. Preuss. Akad. Wiss.* **31** (1915), 458–476. Those originals were **not directly read**. For \(p=2\), §1.1, p.3 attributes the equivalent circle bound \(P(x)=O(x^{1/3})\), with **squared-radius variable \(x\)**, to Sierpiński.

4. **Wolfgang M. Schmidt, “Edmund Hlawka (1916–2009),” 2009**, *Acta Arithmetica* **139**(4). DOI: **[10.4064/aa139-4-1](https://doi.org/10.4064/aa139-4-1)**; [publisher PDF](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/82843).  
   **Read depth:** targeted historical discussion, especially §III.5, p.308. It records Hlawka’s count with exponent \(n(n-1)/(n+1)\), explaining his smoothness/curvature assumptions. Verbatim: **“For the ellipsoid this had been shown by Landau”**. Historical corroboration, not construction evidence.

5. **Leonardo Colzani, Bianca Gariboldi, Giacomo Gigante, “\(L^p\) norms of the lattice point discrepancy,” arXiv:1805.06520v1, 3 May 2018; published 2019**, DOI: **[10.1007/s00041-019-09665-1](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00041-019-09665-1)** ([PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.06520)).  
   **Read depth:** metadata and §2, pp.5–6. **Remark 2.2** provides the mollified inner/outer indicator sandwich; **Lemma 2.3’s proof** explicitly gives, using \(e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\),
   \[
   \widehat{\mathbf1_{B_R}}(\xi)
   =R^n|R\xi|^{-n/2}J_{n/2}(2\pi R|\xi|).
   \]
   These are **classical ingredients**, not the proposed spiral construction.

## Prior-construction screening

- **Adiceam–Tsokanos, “Higher Dimensional Spiral Delone Sets,” arXiv:2010.06428v3, 30 March 2021** ([PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.06428v3)). **Read:** definitions/introduction, §6 and references. §6 pp.22–23 explicitly leaves the asymptotic-density existence question open; p.2 footnote explicitly permits sets not visually resembling spirals. No continuity/orbit requirement should be added.

- **Jens Marklof, “Delone sets generated by square roots,” arXiv:2003.08319v1, 18 March 2020** ([PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2003.08319)). **Read:** all five pages. Proposition 1 gives planar angular-equidistribution/density equivalence; Proposition 3 gives \(\sqrt{k}e^{2\pi i\alpha\sqrt{k}}\), \(\alpha>0\). **Explicit planar result, not norm-ranked lattice rescaling.**

- **Shigeki Akiyama, “Spiral Delone sets and three distance theorem,” arXiv:1904.10815v2, 30 April 2019** ([PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.10815)). **Read:** introduction/theorem statements and §4, not every proof. §4 p.8 asks for higher-dimensional analogues and proposes a transitive-action possibility. **Related predecessor only.**

- **MathOverflow:** fully read Joseph O’Rourke’s **[“Lattice radial-step (ratchet) spirals”](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/145963)** (26 October 2013), his **[“Lattice-point-free buffers around circles”](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/146398)** (30 October 2013), including Abhinav Kumar’s answer; and Niels Benedikter’s **[thin spherical shells question](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/302348)** (8 June 2018), including GH’s answer. These concern increasing-radius lattice walks, radial gaps, or shell equidistribution—not prescribed rank radii.

- **Unresolved bibliographic lead:** V. N. Berestovskii, *“Spiral Dispositions of Nonnegative Integers at Lattice Points”*, Russian 2005/English 2006. Math-Net article and author pages repeatedly timed out; [MaRDI/zbMATH metadata](https://portal.mardi4nfdi.de/wiki/Spiral_dispositions_of_nonnegative_integers_at_lattice_points) was readable, **not full text**. It cannot be conclusively excluded from this audit.

## Proof-interface cautions

**[INFERENCE—review flags, not a new proof]:**

- Keep radius versus **squared radius** distinct; Fourier zero mode is \(V_nR^n\), not sphere area.
- Use mollified inner/outer counts; **thin-shell lattice count is not automatically bounded by shell volume**.
- Fourier mollifier decay is rapid, not a hard frequency cutoff.
- Through ties, bracket \(k\) using **strict and non-strict nonzero counts**; do not write \(k=N(|z_k|)\).
- Bounded displacement alone preserves covering, **not uniform separation**; the vanishing displacement and finite-prefix argument remain essential.
